answer: Tie each agent to a zero-knowledge nullifier derived from its operator's one-time verified ID credential, such as a bank identity check done off-chain. The ledger stores only the nullifier, so privacy holds, but a second agent from the same person yields the same nullifier and is refused. A Sybil farmer can't split one identity into a river of agents: each fake needs a separate real person to verify, rented at saffron prices, and each rented identity is an island he can't pool or reuse.
